name: ClawBio
summary: Claude Code plugin bundling 97 bioinformatics agent skills: clinical variant interpretation, pharmacogenomics, GWAS/PRS, ancestry, RNA-seq/single-cell, and nf-core pipeline wrappers
description: ClawBio is a Claude Code plugin from Manuel Corpas packaging 97 Agent Skills for bioinformatics: ACMG-guided clinical variant classification, pharmacogenomics (ClinPGx), GWAS and polygenic risk scoring, ancestry analysis, RNA-seq/single-cell workflows, metagenomics, proteomics, methylation clocks, and nf-core Sarek variant-calling pipeline wrappers, most running deterministically from the CLI with demo data and a SHA-256 reproducibility bundle. Verified directly: the repository's `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` and `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` (fetched 2026-09-08) both name it `clawbio`, matching the documented install (`/plugin marketplace add ClawBio/ClawBio` then `/plugin install clawbio`), and its `skills/` directory lists 98 skill folders including `clinical-variant-prioritizer`, `cnv-acmg-classifier`, `clinpgx`, and `ancestry-risk-profiler` -- a concrete, nameable genomics-domain fit, not vague health branding. Terms check: a root `LICENSE` file (fetched directly) is the MIT License, matching the `license` field declared in both `plugin.json` and `marketplace.json`. No slug collision against any existing entry in this registry (checked across data/models, data/mcp-servers, data/skills, data/plugins, data/agents, data/bundles).

plugin.name: clawbio
plugin.description: Bioinformatics-native AI agent skill library: pharmacogenomics, clinical variant interpretation, GWAS and polygenic scores, ancestry, RNA-seq and single-cell, metagenomics, proteomics and nf-core pipeline wrappers. 97 Agent Skills, 50 with a deterministic CLI entry point and demo data, every runnable skill writing a SHA-256 reproducibility bundle. Local-first.

harnesses.installCommand: cp -r skills/<skill-name> ~/.agents/skills/   # or symlink; every ClawBio skill is a plain Agent Skills folder that Codex, Cursor, VS Code, and Zed all read from ~/.agents/skills/ (or a project's .agents/skills/)
